title: 1997 AHSME Problem 24
statement: A rising number, such as \(34689,\) is a positive integer each digit of which is larger than each of the digits to its left. There are \(\binom95=126\) five-digit rising numbers. When these numbers are arranged from smallest to largest, the \(97\)th number in the list does not contain the digit

solutions.text: There are \(\binom84=70\) beginning with \(1.\) Among those beginning with \(2,\) the first \(\binom63=20\) begin with \(23,\) occupying positions \(71\)–\(90.\) Thus the \(97\)th overall is the seventh beginning with \(24:\) \[ \begin{gathered} 24567,24568,24569,24578,\\ 24579,24589,24678. \end{gathered} \] The number \(24678\) omits \(5,\) so B is correct.
hints: Count how many rising numbers begin with \(1\), then with \(23\)
After those blocks, list the first few numbers beginning with \(24\)
